title: René Avila's Afro Cuban Band [Two Sets!]
description: René Avila band leader for a traditional Cuban Charanga band. He has two ensembles, from a trio to a 9 piece band. We have played for Chicago's Summerdance, Navy Pier's Beer Garden, Old Town School of Folk Music and various festivals throughout the city. Our ensembles play traditional Cuban from the golden ages of the 40's 50's and 60's still keeping the "Charanga" format.Charanga is a classical chamber ensemble that came out of Haiti, featuring the unique sound of the french flute and violins. During the Haitian revolution of 1804, this sound migrated to eastern Cuba where it reached Santiago. In the space of 120 years, the modern Charanga was born by adding elements of Africa, Spain, Haiti and Cuba transforming it into an electric mix of cultures and one of the worlds most exciting dance genres.

title: Cannibal Holocaust
description:
DIRECTED BY
Ruggero Deodato
WRITTEN BY
Gianfranco Clerici,
Giorgio Stegani
STARRING
Robert Kerman,
Francesca Ciardi,
Perry Pirkanen
Deep within the heart of the Amazon, a rescue mission uncovers a chilling discovery: reels of raw footage left behind by a vanished documentary crew. Their original quest was to investigate rumors of cannibalistic tribes—but what they captured on film reveals something far more horrifying than legend. Blurring the line between fact and fiction, this controversial cult classic shocked audiences worldwide with its brutal realism and unflinching critique of Western exploitation. Banned in over 50 countries and still notorious decades later, it remains one of the most provocative and unsettling films ever made.
Grindhouse Releasing has restored every shocking frame of CANNIBAL HOLOCAUST for this special edition, which presents the Alan Yates “Green Inferno” documentary footage directly from the original 16mm camera negative in its native aspect ratio of 1.37:1 for the very first time.
“It’s a whole new and perhaps even more powerful experience watching the movie this way, with the alternating aspect ratios,” said Grindhouse Releasing owner Bob Murawski. “This is essentially the same way we constructed Orson Welles’ long-unfinished masterpiece THE OTHER SIDE OF THE WIND.”

title: Created Equal: The Premises and Promises of the Declaration of Independence
location: Regenstein Library, The Special Collections Research Center
description:
On July 2, 1776, the Continental Congress voted to declare independence from Great Britain. Two days later, delegates in Philadelphia finalized a document designed to announce and explain that act to readers in America and Europe.
 The Declaration of Independence asserted the revolutionary right of a people to alter or abolish a government, grounding that principle in the “self-evident” claims that “all Men are created Equal, that they are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights” and “that among these are Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness.”
 Over time, many readers have come to consider the radical philosophical premises in the Declaration as founding political promises of the United States. In doing so, they transformed an indictment of the British King and a manifesto of secession from the British Empire into an American charter of liberty, equality, and rights.
 But the Declaration’s meaning has never been solitary. From the start, readers disagreed about what its authors intended. Since 1776, radically different interpretations of the Declaration’s ideas have been put to different ends—from demands for the legal, political, and social equality of all persons, to claims for the rights of states to secede from the union, to calls for the revolutionary overthrow of the government.
 How did the Declaration’s premises become its promises? Drawing on rare materials from the seventeenth century to the present, this exhibition invites you to explore the document’s meanings in its own time, to consider contested interpretations across history, and to reflect on what the Declaration means today.
 Curator
 Eric Slauter, Associate Professor, Department of English Language and Literature; Associate faculty member, Divinity School; Founding Director of the Karla Scherer Center for the Study of American Culture; The University of Chicago

Visitors to the University of Chicago Library may obtain an entry pass by checking in at Regenstein Library’s entry desk and presenting a current, government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license, CityKey, state ID, or passport to confirm identity. Get more visitor information.
 Exhibition Gallery Hours: Weekdays, 9 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

title: Sewn as One
description:
Sewn as One is a textile installation by the Science, Art, and Sustainability (SAS) team of the Phoenix Sustainability Initiative (PSI), in partnership with Creative Chicago Reuse Exchange (CCRx). On view in the 2nd Floor South Cantilever Lounge at the Logan Center for the Arts.
 The Phoenix Sustainability Initiative (PSI) is a student-led organization at the University of Chicago dedicated to promoting environmental awareness and integrating sustainable practices throughout campus and surrounding communities. Through collaborative partnerships, inclusive community-building, and creative approaches to environmental challenges, PSI encourages students to develop the skills and collective agency necessary to enact tangible change. Its Science, Art, and Sustainability
 (SAS) project group brings these commitments into artistic practice, exploring how material reuse, collective making, and creative experimentation can cultivate environmental responsibility and meaningful connections.
 Collaborating with Creative Chicago Reuse Exchange, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that redistributes donated surplus materials for artists, hobbyists, and educators, the SAS project group transforms upcycled fabrics into a tapestry of collective care and environmental awareness. Through a series of open, hands-on mending workshops, the project invites participants to reconsider mark-making not only as gaining technical skill, but as a social and ecological practice.
 Over the course of two academic quarters, three-hour “Sewing Sunday” sessions were held by SAS and open to anyone on campus or passing through the work space, encouraging both experienced makers and first-time participants to sew, patch, embroider, and mend donated textiles. Each contribution—a series of stitching, patchwork, or conversation—becomes part of the evolving textured surface of the work.
 The accumulated labor, dialogue, experimentation, and learning from these sessions culminated into the large-scale fabric installation that spans the hallway of Logan Center for the Arts’ South Cantilever Lounge. The final tapestries act as visual records of foregrounding sustainability, slow making, and community engagement while tracing how individual acts of care can coalesce into an exuberant, communicative form.

title: Time, Fragmented
description:
Time, Fragmented asks what it means for a place to be shaped by complex social and environmental histories, and how distinct but interrelated histories coalesce to create a collective narrative. Along these lines, the exhibition considers contemporary practices of unearthing, both literally and figuratively, and investigates remnants of times past, piecing together the story that unfolds thereafter. In the context of shifting regional powers and migrating stories, Time, Fragmented illuminates the (hi)stories foundational to modern-day Turkey, tracing diasporas of culture, thought, and practice.
 Materials entail historic postcards and photographs from the turn of the twentieth century displayed from a family collection by İbrahim Selim Ergöz. Additionally, building and ornamental materials from the Joel Snyder Materials Collection are displayed alongside photographs and maps from historic expeditions from the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Archives. Finally, multi-media works from New Orleans-based Turkish artist, Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes are presented alongside personal ephemera from the artist and curator. Through a variety of items from polyphonic sources, Time, Fragmented engages with the many layers of history—witnessed through a mosaic of lived reality, filtered through glimpses of past experiences—that live in time.
 Curator
 Time, Fragmented is curated by Defne Ergöz, BA/MA ’27, an Environment, Geography, and Urbanization major and Architectural Studies minor in the College, concurrently pursuing an MA in Art History.
 Artists
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes (Turkish, b. 1997)
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes lives and works in New Orleans, Louisiana since 2024. Türkoğlu Hewes is a conceptual photographer, building worlds for a single frame that carry the immaterial nature of emotions to a physical realm, portraying their silent dictate on lived experiences. The artist focuses on conflicting collective and personal agendas, evaluating dynamics between discipline and intuition, culture and callings. Her Turkish identity and upbringing rooted in strong familial ties appears in her recent work completed in İstanbul. The coexistence of culture and nature in her work criticizes the misconception of full control over emotional environments, similar to the power assumed over natural ecosystems. Türkoğlu Hewes studied fine arts, film and theater at Northwestern University. Her work has been exhibited in the 2025 Louisiana Contemporary at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art. She has been included in exhibitions at Soho Photo Gallery in New York City, Barın Han in İstanbul, and the Contemporary Art Center in New Orleans.
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz (Turkish, b. 1971)
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz, the curator’s father, currently resides in Westchester, New York. Ergöz has been collecting antique ephemera since he was fifteen, with a vast collection spanning his interests in historical documentation and postal items, especially as it concerns the Middle East North Africa region. His archive ranges from widely-available materials to rare collectibles. Time, Fragmented is the first instance Ergöz’s collection will be on public display.
 Support
 CWAC Exhibitions is organized by the Department of Art History’sVisual Resources Center. Additional support for the exhibition is provided by the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures, the Committee on Environment, Geography, and Urbanization, the Master of Arts Program in the Humanities, and Architectural Studies.
 The CWAC Exhibitions team includes Katie Chen, Scarlet Ding, Jiayi Laura Feng, Natalie Hsu, Grace Newby, Kseniya Portnaya, Stephanie Strother, and Yanlin Zhu.

title: Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive
description:
Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive brings together album covers, book jackets, magazines, film stills, photographs, prints, and other ephemera featuring the work of Charles White (1918-1979) to examine the expansive cultural life of his imagery. Tracing how his work circulated beyond the studio and the museum wall, the exhibition reveals how White’s images centered everyday life and shaped a broader visual language.
 An artist who worked fluidly across drawing, painting, printmaking, and mural-making, White created what he described as “powerful images of dignity”, centering African-American experiences as well as historical figures and events at a time when such representations were widely distorted or excluded from mainstream culture. These opportunities for reproduction arose through active collaboration with musicians, writers, and filmmakers. White’s images were adapted, printed, and distributed across a wide range of media, crossing disciplines and communities to become part of a shared cultural consciousness.
 By foregrounding circulation alongside creation, the exhibition invites visitors to consider how White’s work contributed to the formation of a Black visual canon. His images did not remain fixed objects behind glass — they became living symbols, connecting people, histories, and communities through a sustained commitment to representation, relationships, and what White himself understood as a sense of oneness.
 Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive is a special initiative of the Charles White Archives presented by Logan Center Exhibitions and the South Side Community Art Center. The exhibition is curated by Ian White with curatorial support by Paulina Alvarez, Jan Brugger, and jada-amina. Additional support is provided by the Ng Family Visiting Artist Fund, the Revada Foundation, and Friends of the Logan Center.

title: Anne Frank The Exhibition
location: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
address: 5700 S Lake Shore Drive, Chicago, IL, 60637
description:
ANNE FRANK: THE EXHIBITIONat Griffin MSI
Anne Frank The Exhibition is an immersive, full-scale recreation of the Annex where Anne Frank, her family and four other Jewish inhabitants lived in hiding during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Griffin Museum of Science and Industry is the first museum in the Midwest to present this exhibition, and Chicago is only the second U.S. city to host this extraordinary experience, featuring never-before-seen artifacts from Anne Frank’s life. 
Explore the world that shaped Anne’s story, from her early childhood in Frankfurt through the rise of Nazi Germany and the spread of antisemitism across Europe, to the Frank family’s move to Amsterdam. There, Anne lived for nearly ten years, including the final two, which were spent in hiding. 
Step inside the meticulously reconstructed Annex and reflect on the daily challenges, risks and courage of those who hid there before their arrest and deportation in 1944.
Anne Frank The Exhibition is a presentation of the Anne Frank House.

title: Down In Front: Saturday Morning Cartoons
description:
Our culture is rotting from within, and it is perhaps most evident in the decline in our observance of tradition. People need ritual to maintain a sense of order in this chaotic world, and it's because of that Down In Front is doing our part to renew one of the most important weekly traditions engaged by the majority of Americans.
We're talking, of course, about **Saturday Morning Cartoons**, tragically phased out of all our lives in the '90s. What other weekly ritual could we be talking about? Down In Front will tackle a handful of cartoons from the good old days after deregulation, when cartoons were really just long commercials interrupted by shorter commercials and breakfast cereals were just colored sugar and shaped marshmallows.
**Pajamas VERY encouraged. All attendees will receive a special breakfast cereal treat. YUM!**

title: Genealogy Session ONLINE
description:
ONLINE EVENT
A Well-Documented Case Study: Swedish Immigrant Enoch Matteson
Speaker: Janet Johnson
Free for Swedish American Genealogical Society members.
Join us for an engaging presentation by Janet Johnson as she demonstrates how thorough research, careful documentation, and persistence can bring an immigrant ancestor's story to life. Through the case study of Swedish immigrant Enoch Matteson, Janet will illustrate the research methods, records, and analytical techniques used to reconstruct an ancestor's journey from Sweden to America.
This presentation will provide valuable insights for genealogists at all levels, showing how a well-documented case study can uncover family relationships, migration patterns, and the historical context that shaped an immigrant's life. Attendees will learn practical strategies for conducting Swedish genealogical research and documenting their findings to genealogical standards.
A native of Michigan's Upper Peninsula, Janet's interest in family history began after interviewing her grandfather, a World War I veteran. The stories he shared sparked a lifelong quest to understand the lives of ordinary people who experienced extraordinary moments in history. Her research journey has taken her on five trips to Sweden and several to Nova Scotia in search of family connections and historical context. Janet is a former President of the Delta County Genealogical Society, founder and leader of the Swedish Genealogy Group of Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Northern Virginia, and Cultural Leader for Drott Lodge of the Vasa Order of America. She recently completed the GenProof course, participated in ProGen, and has attended numerous Swedish American Genealogist (SAG) Conferences. She has also developed and organized two genealogical conferences for the Vasa Order of America.
Her speaking engagements have included presentations for Drott Lodge and District 9 of the Vasa Order of America, the Fairfax Genealogy Society, the Sons of Norway in Washington, D.C., and the Escanaba Public Library.
Most notably, Janet is known for her exceptional research skills and her dedication to helping others improve their genealogical techniques. Although she does not speak Swedish, she has become highly accomplished in Swedish genealogy through extensive use of Swedish records, databases, and research methodologies.
Whether you are researching Swedish ancestors or seeking to strengthen your own genealogical research skills, this presentation will provide valuable lessons in evidence-based family history research.
Register today and discover how one immigrant's story can illuminate the path to your own family's past.

title: Intentionality, 1960: Whose Dreams? Gallery Hours
description:
Arts + Public Life at the University of Chicago presents Intentionality, 1960: Whose Dreams? a new exhibition by Chicago artist Candace Hunter centered on the construction of the Dan Ryan Expressway and the Black communities displaced in its path. Now embedded within Chicago’s physical and social fabric, the Dan Ryan Expressway obscures both the choices that produced it and the lives reorganized around it. The construction disrupted the ordinary intimacies through which a place becomes home: routes traveled, neighbors known, businesses frequented, porches gathered on.
 Through photographic collage, architectural fragments, archival materials, sound, sculptural interventions, and oral histories, Hunter moves between what is documented and what is remembered. The work resists the idea that displacement can be understood solely through statistics.
 The series builds on the Memory Teas Candace hosted during her APL residency, which gathered first-person accounts from Black Chicagoans who remember the Dan Ryan’s construction and the neighborhoods transformed by it. Rather than asking these memories to complete the historical record, Hunter allows them to stay partial, layered, and unresolved.
 While centered on Chicago’s South Side, the history at the heart of Intentionality, 1960 reaches beyond the city. Across the United States, highway construction, redevelopment, and urban renewal reshaped Black communities, often presenting profound social and spatial disruption as necessary progress. Intentionality, 1960 invites audiences to see those histories not as isolated events but as part of a larger American story.
 Intentionality, 1960 will be accompanied by Threshold: Conversations on the Stoop, a series of public dialogues on the front porch within the exhibition between Candace and scholars to dive into topics related to the exhibition. The Threshold conversations are presented with support from the Office of the Provost Diversity and Inclusion team, in partnership with the Chicago Forum for Free Inquiry and Expression.
 Intentionality, 1960: Whose Dreams? will be on view from September 24-December 12 in the Arts + Public Life Gallery Space located in the Arts Incubator at 301 E. Garfield Blvd.
 Gallery Hours: Thursday-Saturday | 1:00 - 5:00pm

title: Raise the Red Lantern
description:
DIRECTED BY
Yimou Zhang
WRITTEN BY
Tong Su,
Ni Zhen
STARRING
Gong Li,
Jingwu Ma,
Saifei He
Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father's death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.
“As visually striking as it is dramatically effective,” Zhang Yimou’s Academy Award-nominated Raise the Red Lantern sumptuously captures 1920s China while “subtly exploring the politics of power and control” (Janet Maslin, The New York Times). One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.
The 4K restoration of Raise the Red Lantern was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong - Bologna).

title: SoundBridge Ensemble
description:
Sat, Nov 28
Friendly Music Community
Music. Community. Purpose.
A Chicago-based musical ensemble dedicated to bringing multi-generational musicians and audiences together through innovative and socially meaningful musical programs.
Nov 28, 2026, 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM
Friendly Music Community, 6731 Roosevelt Rd, Berwyn, IL 60402, USA
SoundBridge is a Chicago-based musical ensemble dedicated to bringing multi-generational musicians and audiences together through innovative and socially meaningful musical programs. Each year, SoundBridge develops and performs a new concert-based musical program centered on a different musical genre, drawing upon the diverse musical backgrounds, experiences, and talents of over a dozen musicians and vocalists.
SoundBridge was founded on the belief that live music is more than entertainment. It is a means of creating community, encouraging cultural understanding, providing artists of all generations with meaningful opportunities for creative expression, and making the arts accessible to people who might otherwise have limited opportunities to experience live musical performances.
Where the Backroads Lead Our current program, “Where the Backroads Lead,” explores the evolution of country music through the generations, from its early roots to contemporary artists. Rather than presenting a chronological journey, we bring country music to life through a narrative lens and the reflections of one individual looking back on his life, his roots, his relationships, and the town that shaped him. Through his personal story, some of country music’s greatest songs give voice to his journey.
Charitable EFFORTS
The ensemble operates through the volunteer participation of musicians and vocalists contributing their time, talent, energy, and emotional investment. Rather than compensating performers, SoundBridge provides musicians with an opportunity to participate in a serious artistic project, develop and share their talents, build community, and contribute to a social cause. All venue proceeds or patron contributions go directly to one of three charities. For this performance season SoundBridge is aligned with St. Jude Hospital, Tutoring Chicago, and The Greater Chicago Food Depository.
Friendly Music Community
The SoundBridge Performance of “Where the Backroads lead” at The Friendly Music Community will be performed to benefit Tutoring Chicago, which has a 61-year history of providing one on one tutoring to financially disadvantaged kids. This year, 1500 kids will benefit from their commitment.

title: Yoahn John Kwon | Frédéric Chopin: The Poet of the Piano
description:
The acclaimed concert pianist Yoahn John Kwon will perform late masterpieces by Frédéric Chopin, including the Waltz, Impromptu, Sonata, Barcarolle, Mazurka, and Ballade.
This concert is made possible through the generosity of the artist’s friends and supporters.
PROGRAM
Waltz in C# minor, Op. 64, No.2
Impromptu No.2 in F # Major, Op. 36
Ballade No.3 in A flat Major, Op.47
Fantasie-Impromptu in C# minor, Op. 66
Barcarolle in F # Major, Op.60
Ballade No.1 in G minor, Op. 23
Mazurka in F minor, Op. 68, No. 4
Sonata No.3 in B minor, Op. 58
Pianist Yoahn John Kwon began his musical journey at the age of nine, quickly demonstrating exceptional talent. He first studied at the Pre-College Division of The Juilliard School before earning both a Bachelor’s and a Master’s degree from Mannes College of Music, where he studied with Diane Walsh and Carl Schachter.
During his formative years, pianist Jacob Krichaf, a disciple of the great pianist Claudio Arrau, guided him. He also received mentorship and lessons from renowned musicians such as Anton Kuerti, Jacques Rouvier, and John O’Conor.
Mr. Kwon later pursued a perfectionnement program (professional development program) at L’école Normale de Musique de Paris with Anne Queffelec for four consecutive years.
A native of South Korea, Mr. Kwon has received widespread acclaim for his profound musicianship, sensitivity, and insightful performances. The respected critic Harris Goldsmith described him as a “versatile and interesting musician who captures audiences’ attention from beginning to end.”
As a soloist, recitalist, and chamber pianist, Mr. Kwon has performed in some of the world’s most prestigious concert halls across Europe, Asia, and North America. He frequently collaborates with members of renowned orchestras, including New York, Seoul, Tokyo, London, Dresden and many others in chamber music concert series.
As a prolific recording artist, he is well regarded for his acclaimed CDs with Sony Classical and the Audioguy label, especially his interpretations of Chopin and Beethoven.
In addition to his concert career, Mr. Kwon is a sought-after teacher, helping prospective students from South Korea. His recent private students have gained admission to several top conservatories and universities worldwide, including the Manhattan School of Music, Mannes College of Music, the Peabody Institute at Johns Hopkins University, Indiana University in Bloomington, Oberlin College, the Cleveland Institute of Music, the Eastman School of Music at the University of Rochester, Northwestern University, USC’s Thornton School of Music, L’École Normale de Musique de Paris, HMDK Stuttgart, Hochschule für Musik Hanns Eisler Berlin, and the MMA Program at Yale University.
Now based in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, Mr. Kwon contributes to the music community in various roles, including concert piano technician (as a graduate of the prestigious Renner Academy), church organist, and chamber music coach. He also serves on the piano faculty at Beloit College in Wisconsin, where he guides the next generation of artists.

title: Whitechapel with Chelsea Grin, The Acacia Strain, and Netherwalker
description:
Hymns in Dissonance, indeed: “No holds barred; there is nothing nice about HID, from the riffs to the lyrics to the overall vibe of the album,” states guitarist Alex Wade. “We attempted to write our heaviest album to date. We wanted to put out something that was shockingly menacing and brutal.”
“The album follows the story of a cultist who is gathering worthy people to join his cult,” Wade furthers, “and there are moments in the storyline where the cult followers are singing an evil hymn to open a portal for the head cultist to enter.” The band’s dynamic, brutal musicality serves as a soundtrack to the compelling lyrical story that vocalist Phil Bozeman vividly imagines.
“Hymns in Dissonance is a mockery of the true nature of what hymns are,” Bozeman explains. “Hymns are melodious and harmonious. Dissonance is the opposite of melody and harmony. Dissonance represents evil. The tracks on the record are the hymns, which represent the seven deadly sins, beginning from Track 3 to Track 10. Tracks one and two are the introduction.”
The lineup’s timely and terrifying vision was first unveiled in Fall 2024 with the single “A Visceral Retch” inciting frenzied fans to call the song “a version of Whitechapel we have never heard before. Can’t explain how absolutely goddamn brutal this song is. This is a total dream come true.” The title track is the LP’s second single.
Whitechapel, who formed in Knoxville, Tennessee, in 2006, has seen the core lineup—vocalist Phill Bozeman; guitarists Ben Savage, Zach Householder and Alex Wade; bassist Gabe Crisp—intact since 2007, with the exception of the drummer Brandon Zackey, who has been playing with the band since 2022. While Hymns in Dissonance follows 2021’s Kin chronologically, the new album is actually somewhat of a sequel to This is Exile thematically, the three-word title Hymns in Dissonance representing that correlation.
Whitechapel started writing for the new album at Householder’s studio in June of 2023, following the band’s headlining tour for The Valley. Whitechapel stuck to a strict weekday schedule, the structure allowing for maximum creativity and minimum burnout. Householder produced Hymns in Dissonance, which allowed the musicians to seamlessly switch gears from preproduction to recording the full album without skipping a beat. The guitarist shadowed producer Mark Lewis a lot over the last five Whitechapel albums and bringing that influence inside the band is a “full circle moment for Householder and Whitechapel. “It’s cool that we can be self-sufficient and produce a record of this magnitude ourselves; not a lot of bands can say that.”
Every detail on HID matters. “With song sequencing we like to try to make our albums as dynamic as possible,” Wade says. “We like to give the records a roller-coaster effect toggling the energy of the tracks up and down to keep the listener interested.” It was likewise critical that the album art tied into the music in a visceral, provocative way, or has Bozeman put it, “something simple but unsettling with a very classic feel. But not over the top with too many things to look at.” Guitarist Savage mocked up ideas for an eerie mask that would represent the cult leader in the album’s story. Whitechapel chose artist Rob Borbas, the European tattoo artist known as “Grind Design,” to create the cover. “He specializes in dark/cryptic tattoos, and we felt he would be able to take Savage’s idea with the mask and bring it to life,” Whitechapel explains. “He certainly met our expectations with a dark, evil, ominous piece that makes you question ‘what is that?’ when you look at it. We wanted the cover to be mysterious until you know more about the story of the album and how the cover applies to it.” Hymns in Dissonance sees the band reinventing themselves, going darker, deeper and heavier. While the songs all stand powerfully on their own, the throughline Bozeman says that “more than likely there will be a tour where we play the album from front to back.”
Longtime fans will detect hints of the past within the brutality. To wit: the riff-tastic “Hate Cult Ritual” is the only song on the album with Drop A tuning, the tuning the first three Whitechapel albums used. Additionally, the Hymns in Dissonance chapter in Bozeman’s life finds the frontman living through his “past times,” or as he states, “the music that brought me here. Brutal, dark, aggressive, heavy music. Death metal, black metal, speed metal, etc. I truly believe that your roots call you back at some point in your life and this is that point in my life.”
Vocally, the recording process allowed Bozeman to achieve all his goals. “Recording was on our time, so if I wasn't feeling it on a certain day, then I’d just stop, reset and go again the following day. I honed in more on the progression of the screaming vocals that I’m known for,” the singer says. “I really reworked my high vocals and tried some new different types of tones with my voice. Basically, a new-age feel to a classic sound.”
At this stage in the game, the name Whitechapel commands the ultimate respect. Already sitting on one of the most enviable catalogs in contemporary metal, in 2019 they dropped The Valley, highlighting a confident evolution in their sound and standing as a true landmark release that sets a new standard for the genre. With Bozeman exploring childhood trauma on 2019’s The Valley, it was their darkest release to-date. But with its 2021 successor, Kin, the story was darker still.
With those chapters of Bozeman’s life exorcised lyrically, Hymns in Dissonance mines a darkness that’s not lyrically personal. And, says Wade, “I don't think HID follows Kin musically at all. If anything, it's the polar opposite. For this album it was fun to be able to just let loose and write ignorantly heavy music again. This album stands on its own,” Wade concludes. “Phil was able to create a fresh story to write about, which, in turn, helped us write music with a fresher sound.”
Lineup:
Phil Bozeman — Vocals
Ben Savage — Guitar
Zach Householder — Guitar
Alex Wade — Guitar
Gabe Crisp — Bass
Brandon Zackey — Drums
Hymns in Dissonance track listing:
Hymns in Dissonance song by song:
Prisoner 666 – This song was the first song we wrote and musically feels like the 2014/2021 Whitechapel morphing back into the 2006-2010 Whitechapel and continuing the 2006-2010 era for the rest of the album. This is the beginning of the narrative of "the last living son" of the Father of Lies coming to be. Relinquishing his faith, religion, burning the church and serving Satan, who he believes is his father. (Phil Bozeman)
It’s got heavy “Saw is the Law” vibes in the opening groove, it’s like we took that song and made it more epic and melodic. The “beats per minute” are pretty similar to Saw. (Alex Wade)
Hymns in Dissonance – It’s about building his cult of followers. Only the most heinous and vile people on the planet. Showing their devotion to their lord. Committing horrible acts and the leader showcasing his power and his purpose. To commit the seven cardinal sins to resurrect their lord. To replace divinity with evil. (Phil Bozeman)
Mostly written by Phil on guitar, it has a few riffs and tweaks thrown in by the rest of us. He can churn out some pummeling riffs and it’s one of the best songs on the album because he had a vision for the whole song with the riffs and vocals. It’s tuned to Drop G which we have been using since the self-titled LP, but the ending breakdown shifts down one whole step to Drop F, which we have never done before. Having the final breakdown shift lower than the rest of the song really helped the end have the crushing feeling it needed. (Alex Wade)
Diabolic Slumber - Sin of Sloth: watching people die and not doing anything to save them. Falling into a deep sleep while the world tears itself apart. No empathy, no feeling. Pure apathy. (Phil Bozeman)
This was a fun song to put together and another one that felt like it just kind of wrote itself. We were just riffing at Zach’s and each part just came one after the other. I like it because it reminds me more of our songwriting back in the day on Somatic Defilement where we had parts that went back-to-back vs a more verse/chorus/bridge type repeating structure. It leaves the listener wondering what is coming next. (Alex Wade)
A Visceral Retch - Sin of Gluttony: mammoth demons constantly gorging themselves and excreting. True followers will gorge on the excrement or their fellow man. A spectacle of entertainment for the cult and finding true devotion to them through horrific means. The path to true madness and impurity. (Phil Bozeman)
Mostly written by Zach, who loves Cannibal Corpse (who doesn’t) and I think that shows in the riffing of this song. Just huge grotesque death metal riffs. It also utilizes some pitch shifting on a whammy pedal where we drop the guitars down and octave and you can hear them dive bombing down. I think that gave it a unique sound that not a lot of death metal songs have. The end also shifts down in tuning to Drop F like the end of Hymns which adds to the brutality to close it out. (Alex Wade)
Ex Infernis - We wanted an evil, ritualistic-sounding instrumental to bring in the next track and Ex Infernis is Latin for "from below/hell." (Phil Bozeman)
Zach created this interlude track using an orchestral drum software. He was able to program every part, from the stick clicks to the banging timpani drums and the monk chants. This track is to symbolize the beginning of the ritual the cultists do to open the portal for the Cult Leader. (Alex Wade)
Hate Cult Ritual - Sin of Wrath: this song portrays the overwhelming rage of the cult. Planting the seed of evil within the core of the earth to be birthed from soil. All the rivers and oceans are diseased which nourishes their unborn lord. Roaming the earth and murdering all opposers. (Phil Bozeman)
This is the only song utilizing our older tuning, Drop A; the rest of the album is in Drop G. I was inspired a lot by Bloodbath when writing this one and felt like Phil nailed the vibe vocally contributing to that. There is a ferocity and evilness to this track that I think really sets it apart from the rest. No breakdowns, just pummeling riffs with evil chanting over the choruses. (Alex Wade)
The Abysmal Gospel - Sin of Pride: portraying the acts of arrogance and superiority. Mocking the divine. The transformation from human to beast. (Phil Bozeman)
This was interesting to create because it felt like a mash-up of riffs that just worked. The intro was written kind of randomly and it was so heavy we were trying to find a place to use it and decided “why not have it open this song then kick straight into the punk/grind riff? It’s pretty diverse, with influences of slam, grind, and melodic metal. We threw it all together and it just worked. (Alex Wade)
Bedlam - Sin of Envy: in the album This is Exile there was a character "Daemon" who is the brother of the cult leader. This song is him admitting his jealousy of him and defiling his rotting corpse. This is the POV of him and his dead brother who is eternally trapped in his own dead body and can still feel and hear everything but cannot move or escape. Bedlam is chaos, confusion and turmoil which describes this scene. (Phil Bozeman)
We wrote this intentionally as a quick, fun, ass-beater type song. It’s pretty relentless with the chunky slamming riffs, but then also has a melodic and catchy chorus as the hook. (Alex Wade)
Mammoth God - Sin of Greed: this portrays the stealing of land and wealth. Conquering every inch of the world. A god of avarice. So overtaken with greed that he wants to kill himself so he can claim to have slayed every god. (Phil Bozeman)
I always felt like this was the “true metal” song of the album, nothing about it really says ‘Deathcore’ to me. It’s an intense track with a lot of dark melody and a killer solo toward the end. Savage added a little ‘rock roll’ flair to the solo that I think makes it unique compared to standard metal solos. (Alex Wade)
Nothing is Coming for Any of Us - Sin of Lust: the earth is bearing his child. The earth is portrayed as a person, a woman bearing the child, their lord. He does not love who is bearing the child. The rest I would rather the listener take away what they will. It's my favorite song on the album; the flow of the song, the vocal variety and lyrical content is what drives me towards that one. Plus, the ending is just very beautiful but unsettling. (Phill Bozeman)
On every album we try to close it out with the most epic song from the 10 we’ve written. It’s kind of our signature to leave the listener with one last “wow” before the album ends. I think this song accomplishes that. Phil wrote most of the riffs on this one too, which I think contributed to it being one of the best on the album. The ending melodies were written by Savage, closing the album in a perfect cathartic way. (Alex Wade)

title: TheARTI$T, GAWD, AMARI NOELLE
description:
TheARTI$T
A product of the infamous city of Newark, NJ TheARTI$T is a rising musician who blends her stories into heartfelt frequencies that string at consumer’s heart’s from the first listen. As her success continues to grow, TheARTI$T has already added herself to the long list of talent from Newark.
Growing up surrounded by music, it’s no surprise that her dreams for global reach and impact have begun to flourish. The most recent traction surrounding her bonafide single Sober comes at a time where the skin in the game that TheARTI$T has put in since 2018 has begun to come to fruition.
As TheARTI$T continues to leverage her ability to turn pain into authentic chords, she will pull out all stops to reach anyone who uses her music to soothe themselves.
GAWD
GAWD is what happens when two background singers decide they’re done standing in the background.
The Los Angeles duo — Alana Linsey and Alayna — spent years building their reputation as some of the most trusted voices behind the mic, singing with artists like Anderson .Paak, Steve Lacy, Willow, Harry Styles, and Duckwrth. If you’ve been to the shows or listened closely to the records, chances are you’ve already heard them.
They just weren’t the ones in the spotlight yet.
When GAWD finally stepped forward, they didn’t ease into it. Their debut show in Los Angeles sold out immediately, dropping alongside their breakout single “Waistside,” and the energy hasn’t slowed since. Their live shows feel somewhere between a concert, a house party, and a sermon — powered by tight harmonies, sharp humor, and the kind of chemistry that only comes from years of singing side by side.
The résumé is already wild. GAWD opened for the Red Hot Chili Peppers on the Unlimited Love Tour with Anderson .Paak & The Free Nationals, supported Duckwrth across 13 international dates, and most recently joined Becky Hill for a run of shows across the U.S. They also served as direct support for Durand Bernarr and contributed vocals to his Grammy-winning album BLOOM.
And the world outside of music is starting to catch on too — including a recent appearance in Anderson .Paak’s directorial film debut K-POPs.
Musically, GAWD lives somewhere between R&B, house, soul, and alternative pop — sensual, playful, a little rebellious, and always honest.
The girls are here.
And with new music arriving and their debut album on the way, they’re just getting warmed up.
AMARI NOELLE
Beginning her career on the Soundcloud scene Million$$Maddy became Amari’Noelle. Hailing from Gary, Indiana Amari was raised by a family of creatives. Growing up watching her musical mother and attending a visual and performing arts academy it was no surprise that Amari would gravitate towards music herself. Transitioning from a basketball star to rising R&B artist Amari’Noelle is putting her all into her new music.
The Gary, Indiana-based artist has released her first single, “Wait For Me,” in December 2021. Inspired by life, self-reflection and relationships, “Wait For Me,” was the start of a whole new journey for Amari’Noelle. Coming from a humble upbringing and not being able to afford studio time or studio equipment Amari records all of her music on her iPhone. To date, she has recorded over 150 songs on her iPhone in 2021 and is ready to continue releasing music off her debut album Amari SZN 1. Emerging as a R&B artist Amari is excited to put forth her best work yet and ready to touch the minds and hearts of her fans.

title: Tommy Davidson
description:
Tommy Davidson's Bio
Tommy Davidson’s exceptional range – from stand-up comedy and acting to versatile music accomplishments – have earned him a reputation as an extraordinary performer who delivers no matter the arena. Best known as one of the stars of the hit television show In Living Color, Davidson’s visibility has allowed him to become a household name known for his innovative talent.
Davidson started his career as a standup comedian in Washington DC, earning an ardent following. Spotted by major concert promoters, he was first booked as the opening act for Patti LaBelle, Kenny G and Luther Vandross. It wasn’t long before he came to Hollywood and was headlining the biggest rooms and met Robert Townsend. This led to his first national tv appearance and starring role in Partners in Crime, the conduit to Keenan Ivory Wayans, who proved instrumental in Davidson’s career by offering him an opportunity to audition.
Davidson starred in Disney Channel’s beloved animated series The Proud Family (2001-05) and recently returned to topline their new hit, “The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder” (Disney +) to rave reviews. Other 2022 guest starring credits include CBS comedy series The Neighborhood; standout roles on VH1’s hit A Black Lady Sketch Show; the Nick Cannon-directed TV movie Miracles Across 125th Street, BET+’s The Ms. Pat Show and the Netflix special Sarah Cooper: Everything’s Fine.
The multihyphenate is perhaps best known for starring in the groundbreaking sketch comedy series In Living Color and becoming a standout with his impressions of Sammy Davis Jr., Michael Jackson and other entertainment icons. His performance on the series resulted in three Showtime specials: On Strength of New York, Illin’ in Philly, and Takin’ it to DC. Davidson also hosted and starred in the network’s Chocolate Sundaes Comedy Show, as well as three seasons of ABC’s Vacation Creation.
Davidson voiced the series regular role of Cream Corn in the Adult Swim action-comedy spoof Black Dynamite, and has also made multiple guest appearances on shows like MTV’s Wild ‘N Out, BET’s Real Husbands of Hollywood and ABC’s Celebrity Wife Swap. He also recently headlined The Off Color Comedy Tour with Keenan Ivory Wayans, Shawn Wayans and David Alan Grier, and co-headlines with Katt Williams, Mike Epps and Martin Lawrence to sell out large venue audiences.
Davidson’s feature credits include Spike Lee’s Bamboozled, Morgan Creek’s Juwanna Mann, Ace Ventura II: When Nature Calls opposite Jim Carrey, and Strictly Business opposite Halle Berry among others. He also recently starred in the feature documentaries I Am Comic opposite Tim Allen and Lewis Black, and Dying Laughing alongside Jamie Foxx, Kevin Hart, Amy Schumer and Sarah Silverman.
His most recent critically lauded music duets include Sweet Reunion with multi-Grammy winner Dave Koz and I Know with A-list saxophonist, Richard Elliot.
Kensington Books published Davidson’s memoir Living in Color: What’s Funny about Me, recounting his personal triumphs after having been abandoned as in infant in 2020 achieving historic sales.

title: A Random Memory: Magic & Mentalism
description:
A Random Memory is an intimate magic and mentalism show worth remembering. Every trick uses the audience's own cares, wishes and memories to create magic with emotional weight. Instead of another round of generic card tricks featuring kings and aces, the show opens with a nearly blank deck of cards and each trick fills out more of the deck with things the audience cares about. To bring things full circle and remind us all that even this show will only be a memory, the audience performs a magic trick of their own that destroys the deck they spent the last hour building.
A Random Memory is the brainchild of magician, Dan Feltey. Dan is a software engineer by trade who fell in love with magic in 2018 and never gave it up. Dan got his start in magic taking classes at Magic Inc., and The Chicago Magic Lounge, before joining Open Heart Magic in 2023 as a bedside magician. Open Heart Magic is a non-profit organization that trains volunteers to perform magic at children's hospitals throughout the midwest, and emphasizes magic that makes the child the center of every trick. Dan brings this philosophy to A Random Memory, allowing the audience to become the star of the show and experience the magic themselves.

title: An Evening With Deacon Blues: Steely Dan Tribute
description:
Deacon Blues was born in the twelfth year of the 21st century. Twelve stellar musicians, composers and educators based in Chicago, they share a unique passion for the Becker/Fagen repository, better known to the world as Steely Dan. Deacon Blues has structured their live repertoire to encompass a wider range of the Dan’s prolific material––all the “hits” are there, but also include rarities as well as repertoire from the Dan’s 1991 reunion prototype––The New York Rock & Soul Revue. In the words of legendary Chicago FM Radio personality Bob Stroud, “If you are a Dan fan, you owe it to yourself to see Deacon Blues — they’ve got all the right musicians with all the right chops — they are an incredible tribute to the music of Steely Dan!”
Under the musical leadership of Steven Kikoen & Thomas Linsk, the group reads as a “who’s who” of world-class musicians. Chicago luminaries and Grammy® winners are either permanent members of the group and/or award-winning featured guests – among them Howard Levy (Kenny Loggins, Paul Simon, Béla Fleck); Paul Wertico (Pat Metheny, Wertico, Cain, & Gray, Time Zone); Richard Patterson (Miles Davis, Michael McDonald, Boz Scaggs, Time Zone); Corky Siegel (Chamber Blues); Ben Johnson & Charles Heath IV (Ramsey Lewis); Wally Hustin (Phoebe Snow, Dave Mason, Mark Stern, David Benoit); Chuck Webb (Aretha Franklin, Ramsey Lewis, & Al Di Meola); Sugar Blue (The Rolling Stones); Billy Branch (The Sons of Blues); Khari Parker (George Benson, Destiny’s Child); Ben Lewis (Gary Sinise’s Lt. dan Band, Ben Lewis Trio, Time Zone); Vijay Tellis-Nayak (Prognosis, Big Suit, Michael Shannon & Jason Narducy and Friends); Cash Michaels (Time Zone); Rich Lapka (Soul Daddy); Victor Garcia (award-winning trumpeter), Thaddeus Tukes (award-winning world-renowned vibraphonist); Char McAllister (Char Dreams); Suzanne Cross (Soul Daddy); Pamela Rose (Encore 33); Elisa Latrice (Simply The Best–Tina Turner); Sally Blandon (Tears dry On Their Own–Amy Winehouse); Jessica Vasilou (Petty Union); and Andrea Miologos (My Weekend Crush).
Buy Now
–– AWARD-WINNING SPECIAL GUESTS AT THIS CONCERT ––
BILLY BRANCH
Billy Branch is an Emmy Award winner, a 3-Time Grammy® Award nominee, and a retired Grammy® governor. He’s won multiple Blues Music Awards (B.M.A.s), most recently winning both the 2026 Best Harmonica Instrumentalist Award and the 2026 Living Blues Critics’ Award. Billy is also a proud recipient of multiple B.M.A. Keeping the Blues Alive Awards for his 45-year-old Blues in the Schools program.
In addition to his numerous humanitarian awards, Branch is most proud of being a 2020 inductee into the Blues Foundation’s Blues Hall of Fame Museum in Memphis. Branch is on the Board of Directors of both the Blues Foundation and the Little Walter Foundation, and is a recipient of an Addy Award — like an Oscar for TV ads — for his on-screen commercial work.
Billy’s recording with Dave Spector is included in the Grammy Museum’s Woody Guthrie installation entitled Songs of Conscience, Sounds of Freedom. Billy is an honored recipient of the 2026 Mellon Foundation’s Taproot Artists & Community Trust Alliance Fellowship, recognizing him as an American Culture-Bearer. He used part of that award to fund a daytime senior citizens’ Blues event on the Southside of Chicago, a Blues in the Schools concert for 500 Chicago students, and a community concert featuring his new album, The Blues Is My Biography.
BERNARD “PRETTY” PURDIE
Original Steely Dan session musician and legendary drummer Bernard “Pretty” Purdie has appeared with Deacon Blues at several of their Arcada and Des Plaines Theatre shows. Native New Jersey resident, legendary drummer and teacher, Bernard is an 84-year-old veteran of the music scene, who started his expansive career with Country Music and went on to Blues, Jazz, Classic Rock, Pop, R & B, and Funk. Bernard has worked with over 2,500 artists and played on over 4,000 records. Bernard’s music finds its roots in the rhythmic sounds of the B&O Railroad trains while growing up in Elkton, Maryland. These roots have taken him around the world, playing, recording, and capturing the sounds and rhythms of the world. Bernard has played every genre of music to thousands of well received audiences.
Bernard’s live work with his band “Bernard Purdie and Friends” in New Jersey featuring Dan Boone, George Naha, Miho Nobuzane-Elijah and frontman Rob Paparozzi has touched the hearts and souls of audiences all around the world. He also has a newly formed band in North Carolina called The Purdie Boys who are Bernard, Chuck Phillips, Bruce Clark & Jesus Vega; rounding out the band are Jim Barbee, Rich Dimetre and Josh Mineer.
Bernard’s work on Broadway & TV Music from the 60’s through the 80’s has left its mark on the Great White Way. His credits include Hair, Two Gentlemen of Verona, and 16 plays by Galt MacDermot. At 84 years of age, he shows no sign of stopping. Bernard Purdie revolutionized drumming with his invention of “The Purdie Shuffle” – inspiring legions and generations of drummers over lo these many years. Bernard has been on more Steely Dan records than any other drummer in history – enjoy the great Bernard Purdie!

title: BTS Express w/ Shirley Johnson
description:
Nicknamed the “Sweetheart 
of the Blues” by the staff at BLUE 
CHICAGO, Shirley has been gracing the stage here since the 1990s with her 
spectacular performances.
Like so many 
African-American vocalists, Shirley Johnson started out singing in church and 
then went on to embrace secular music. The Chicago resident, whose influences 
range from Mahalia Jackson to Koko Taylor, Etta James, and Ruth Brown, is a 
gritty, big-voiced blues singer who can also handle soul and gospel. Although 
Johnson has spent much of her adult life in Chicago, the Windy City is not her 
hometown; she was born in 
Franklin, VA and raised in Norfolk, VA. Shirley came from a very religious 
family and was only six when she 
started singing gospel in a church choir.
When Shirley 
reached adulthood in the late '70s, she pursued a career in secular music and 
made her presence felt in Norfolk's blues and R&B circles. She went on to 
become an opening act for Aretha Franklin, Jerry Butler, Z.Z. Hill, and other 
well-known artists who were passing through town. In the early '80s, she 
recorded some singles for two regional labels in Virginia and those recordings 
caught the attention of a man who was planning to start a label in Chicago. The 
aspiring record man expressed interest in recording Ms. Johnson and sent her a 
plane ticket to Chicago, but when she arrived in the Windy City she learned he 
didn't have enough money to pay for a session.
Nonetheless, she 
decided to remain in Chicago and became active on the city's blues circuit, 
where she has performed both Blues and Soul. The musicians she worked with in

description:
Join us for just $25! Secure your seat in advance, or grab your ticket at the door for $30 (if available; advance purchase highly recommended)
$25 General Admission is a relaxed, free-flowing late-night blues set where artists stretch out, special guests musicians often sit in.

- All sales are final. No refunds -
John Primer: A Chicago Blues Living Legend
John Primer has undisputedly helped shape the sound and style of Chicago blues. The echoes of tradition from the birthplaces he played, such as Maxwell Street, Theresa's, Checkerboard, and Rosa's Lounge, can be heard in every chord he plays. John Primer is a true Chicago Blues Living Legend.
Born in 1945 on a Mississippi sharecropper's land, Primer was inspired by his family's hard work, field songs, and the blues. His dream was to one day play with the legendary Muddy Waters.
In 1963, Primer moved to Chicago and began his journey to becoming a great bluesman. He started with a steady gig at the legendary Maxwell Street and then played seven nights a week for seven years at the famous Theresa's Lounge, where he was taught by the founding fathers of the blues.
Primer's talent caught the attention of Willie Dixon, who took him on tour with his Chicago Blues All-Stars Band. In 1981, Primer's dream came true when he got to play with Muddy Waters, who called him to lead his band, a life-changing experience.
After Muddy's passing, Primer joined Magic Slim & The Teardrops for 14 years, traveling the world. In 1995, he began leading his own band, The Real Deal Blues Band. Primer has been recorded on more than 87 albums, with 17 under his own name, and has written and produced over 55 songs.
Primer's contributions to the blues have been widely recognized. He has received two Grammy Award nominations, two Lifetime Achievement Awards, been inducted into the Chicago Blues Hall of Fame, awarded the "Muddy Award," and won numerous Blues Music Awards and Blues Blast Awards. John Primer is a true Chicago Blues Icon, whose music continues to inspire and captivate audiences worldwide.

title: South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut
description:
DIRECTED BY
Trey Parker
WRITTEN BY
Trey Parker,
Matt Stone,
Pam Brady
STARRING
Trey Parker,
Matt Stone,
Mary Kay Bergman
Towards the end of the last century, concerns mounted over the effect of cartoons on children’s minds. Parents across America reached for the remote when shows like The Simpsons, Ren & Stimpy, or Beavis and Butt-Head came on. But one cartoon drew more revulsion than the rest. And that was South Park—a program as inflammatory as it was intelligent (and remains so to this day). The big screen feature adaptation, South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, depicts and head-on attacks such outsized puritanical outrage when the release of an R-rated animated movie in the fictional mountain town generates accusations of corrupting youth, and a mom-led backlash soon threatens to begin both World War III and the Biblical Apocalypse. Only Stan, Kyle, Kenny, and Cartman can save the day. Filmmakers Trey Parker and Matt Stone teamed with theatre composer Marc Shaiman to craft a world-class, crass, raunchy, Oscar-nominated movie musical—which acted as the perfect antidote to a decade of the Disney Animated Renaissance. Far and away, this is the smartest, funniest, and most culturally resonant movie you’ll ever see with a song about having sex with your uncle. Vive la Résistance!

title: Created Equal: The Premises and Promises of the Declaration of Independence
location: Regenstein Library, The Special Collections Research Center
description:
On July 2, 1776, the Continental Congress voted to declare independence from Great Britain. Two days later, delegates in Philadelphia finalized a document designed to announce and explain that act to readers in America and Europe.
 The Declaration of Independence asserted the revolutionary right of a people to alter or abolish a government, grounding that principle in the “self-evident” claims that “all Men are created Equal, that they are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights” and “that among these are Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness.”
 Over time, many readers have come to consider the radical philosophical premises in the Declaration as founding political promises of the United States. In doing so, they transformed an indictment of the British King and a manifesto of secession from the British Empire into an American charter of liberty, equality, and rights.
 But the Declaration’s meaning has never been solitary. From the start, readers disagreed about what its authors intended. Since 1776, radically different interpretations of the Declaration’s ideas have been put to different ends—from demands for the legal, political, and social equality of all persons, to claims for the rights of states to secede from the union, to calls for the revolutionary overthrow of the government.
 How did the Declaration’s premises become its promises? Drawing on rare materials from the seventeenth century to the present, this exhibition invites you to explore the document’s meanings in its own time, to consider contested interpretations across history, and to reflect on what the Declaration means today.
 Curator
 Eric Slauter, Associate Professor, Department of English Language and Literature; Associate faculty member, Divinity School; Founding Director of the Karla Scherer Center for the Study of American Culture; The University of Chicago
 Visitors
 This exhibition is free and open to all. Visitors to the University of Chicago Library may obtain an entry pass by checking in at Regenstein Library’s entry desk and presenting a current, government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license, CityKey, state ID, or passport to confirm identity. Get more visitor information.
 Exhibition Gallery Hours: Weekdays, 9 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

title: Sewn as One
description:
Sewn as One is a textile installation by the Science, Art, and Sustainability (SAS) team of the Phoenix Sustainability Initiative (PSI), in partnership with Creative Chicago Reuse Exchange (CCRx). On view in the 2nd Floor South Cantilever Lounge at the Logan Center for the Arts.
 The Phoenix Sustainability Initiative (PSI) is a student-led organization at the University of Chicago dedicated to promoting environmental awareness and integrating sustainable practices throughout campus and surrounding communities. Through collaborative partnerships, inclusive community-building, and creative approaches to environmental challenges, PSI encourages students to develop the skills and collective agency necessary to enact tangible change. Its Science, Art, and Sustainability
 (SAS) project group brings these commitments into artistic practice, exploring how material reuse, collective making, and creative experimentation can cultivate environmental responsibility and meaningful connections.
 Collaborating with Creative Chicago Reuse Exchange, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that redistributes donated surplus materials for artists, hobbyists, and educators, the SAS project group transforms upcycled fabrics into a tapestry of collective care and environmental awareness. Through a series of open, hands-on mending workshops, the project invites participants to reconsider mark-making not only as gaining technical skill, but as a social and ecological practice.
 Over the course of two academic quarters, three-hour “Sewing Sunday” sessions were held by SAS and open to anyone on campus or passing through the work space, encouraging both experienced makers and first-time participants to sew, patch, embroider, and mend donated textiles. Each contribution—a series of stitching, patchwork, or conversation—becomes part of the evolving textured surface of the work.
 The accumulated labor, dialogue, experimentation, and learning from these sessions culminated into the large-scale fabric installation that spans the hallway of Logan Center for the Arts’ South Cantilever Lounge. The final tapestries act as visual records of foregrounding sustainability, slow making, and community engagement while tracing how individual acts of care can coalesce into an exuberant, communicative form.

title: Time, Fragmented
description:
Time, Fragmented asks what it means for a place to be shaped by complex social and environmental histories, and how distinct but interrelated histories coalesce to create a collective narrative. Along these lines, the exhibition considers contemporary practices of unearthing, both literally and figuratively, and investigates remnants of times past, piecing together the story that unfolds thereafter. In the context of shifting regional powers and migrating stories, Time, Fragmented illuminates the (hi)stories foundational to modern-day Turkey, tracing diasporas of culture, thought, and practice.
 Materials entail historic postcards and photographs from the turn of the twentieth century displayed from a family collection by İbrahim Selim Ergöz. Additionally, building and ornamental materials from the Joel Snyder Materials Collection are displayed alongside photographs and maps from historic expeditions from the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Archives. Finally, multi-media works from New Orleans-based Turkish artist, Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes are presented alongside personal ephemera from the artist and curator. Through a variety of items from polyphonic sources, Time, Fragmented engages with the many layers of history—witnessed through a mosaic of lived reality, filtered through glimpses of past experiences—that live in time.
 Curator
 Time, Fragmented is curated by Defne Ergöz, BA/MA ’27, an Environment, Geography, and Urbanization major and Architectural Studies minor in the College, concurrently pursuing an MA in Art History.
 Artists
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes (Turkish, b. 1997)
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes lives and works in New Orleans, Louisiana since 2024. Türkoğlu Hewes is a conceptual photographer, building worlds for a single frame that carry the immaterial nature of emotions to a physical realm, portraying their silent dictate on lived experiences. The artist focuses on conflicting collective and personal agendas, evaluating dynamics between discipline and intuition, culture and callings. Her Turkish identity and upbringing rooted in strong familial ties appears in her recent work completed in İstanbul. The coexistence of culture and nature in her work criticizes the misconception of full control over emotional environments, similar to the power assumed over natural ecosystems. Türkoğlu Hewes studied fine arts, film and theater at Northwestern University. Her work has been exhibited in the 2025 Louisiana Contemporary at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art. She has been included in exhibitions at Soho Photo Gallery in New York City, Barın Han in İstanbul, and the Contemporary Art Center in New Orleans.
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz (Turkish, b. 1971)
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz, the curator’s father, currently resides in Westchester, New York. Ergöz has been collecting antique ephemera since he was fifteen, with a vast collection spanning his interests in historical documentation and postal items, especially as it concerns the Middle East North Africa region. His archive ranges from widely-available materials to rare collectibles. Time, Fragmented is the first instance Ergöz’s collection will be on public display.
 Support
 CWAC Exhibitions is organized by the Department of Art History’sVisual Resources Center. Additional support for the exhibition is provided by the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures, the Committee on Environment, Geography, and Urbanization, the Master of Arts Program in the Humanities, and Architectural Studies.
 The CWAC Exhibitions team includes Katie Chen, Scarlet Ding, Jiayi Laura Feng, Natalie Hsu, Grace Newby, Kseniya Portnaya, Stephanie Strother, and Yanlin Zhu.
 Related Programming
 Opening Celebration, Cochrane-Woods Art Center, Wednesday, October 21, 6:00 PM

 CWAC Exhibitions is committed to accessibility for all our exhibitions. However, the second floor of the Cochrane-Woods Art Center is accessible only by stairs. To request an accommodation or alternative format, please email visualresources@uchicago.edu.

title: Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive
description:
Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive brings together album covers, book jackets, magazines, film stills, photographs, prints, and other ephemera featuring the work of Charles White (1918-1979) to examine the expansive cultural life of his imagery. Tracing how his work circulated beyond the studio and the museum wall, the exhibition reveals how White’s images centered everyday life and shaped a broader visual language.
 An artist who worked fluidly across drawing, painting, printmaking, and mural-making, White created what he described as “powerful images of dignity”, centering African-American experiences as well as historical figures and events at a time when such representations were widely distorted or excluded from mainstream culture. These opportunities for reproduction arose through active collaboration with musicians, writers, and filmmakers. White’s images were adapted, printed, and distributed across a wide range of media, crossing disciplines and communities to become part of a shared cultural consciousness.
 By foregrounding circulation alongside creation, the exhibition invites visitors to consider how White’s work contributed to the formation of a Black visual canon. His images did not remain fixed objects behind glass — they became living symbols, connecting people, histories, and communities through a sustained commitment to representation, relationships, and what White himself understood as a sense of oneness.
 Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive is a special initiative of the Charles White Archives presented by Logan Center Exhibitions and the South Side Community Art Center. The exhibition is curated by Ian White with curatorial support by Paulina Alvarez, Jan Brugger, and jada-amina. Additional support is provided by the Ng Family Visiting Artist Fund, the Revada Foundation, and Friends of the Logan Center.

title: Anne Frank The Exhibition
location: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
address: 5700 S Lake Shore Drive, Chicago, IL, 60637
description:
ANNE FRANK: THE EXHIBITIONat Griffin MSI
Anne Frank The Exhibition is an immersive, full-scale recreation of the Annex where Anne Frank, her family and four other Jewish inhabitants lived in hiding during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Griffin Museum of Science and Industry is the first museum in the Midwest to present this exhibition, and Chicago is only the second U.S. city to host this extraordinary experience, featuring never-before-seen artifacts from Anne Frank’s life. 
Explore the world that shaped Anne’s story, from her early childhood in Frankfurt through the rise of Nazi Germany and the spread of antisemitism across Europe, to the Frank family’s move to Amsterdam. There, Anne lived for nearly ten years, including the final two, which were spent in hiding. 
Step inside the meticulously reconstructed Annex and reflect on the daily challenges, risks and courage of those who hid there before their arrest and deportation in 1944.
Anne Frank The Exhibition is a presentation of the Anne Frank House.

title: ISAC Short Class: Imagining and Re-Imagining Homer
description:
Sundays, 10:00–10:30 AM, November 29–December 20), pre-recorded episodes drop every Sunday by 10:00 am
 Instructor: Tasha Vorderstrasse, PhD, Manager, Continuing Education Program, ISAC
 Join us for this ISAC short class on the interpretations and re-interpretations of Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey. Each short class will examine a particular art work and place it in its historical context to see what this tells us about the interpretations and re-interpretations of Homer.
 Week One: Murder of Agamemnon on a Greek red-figure vase and other ancient Greek depictions of Homer
 Week Two: A statue of Penelope at Persepolis in Iran and connections between the Achaemenids and the Greeks
 Week Three: A Gandharan relief of the Trojan Horse and how Greek materials travelled to Afghanistan/northwest Pakistan
 Week Four: Robert Duncanson’s Land of the Lotus Eaters. Explore later interpretations of Homer, focusing on Duncanson’s re-imaging of the scene in the Odyssey based on Tennyson’s poem.
 This class is pre-recorded.

title: A Midsummer Night’s Dream
description:
“Give me your hands, if we be friends”
Sparkling with the festive spirit of the holiday season, Shakespeare’s magical romantic comedy is a delectable treat for the entire family. A snowy Athens gives way to the warm and colorful dream of a midsummer forest as Shakespeare’s best-loved characters are consumed by the absurd chaos of love and the joy of friendship. Young love collides with a fairy feud and a bumbling group of amateur theatricals in the most warm-hearted play in the English language. An enchanting story of love, marriage, and magic, this holiday “Dream” will fill you with happiness and hope.
For the first time in CST’s history, two plays will be performed in repertory by one masterfully talented Chicago Shakespeare Company of actors. Under the creative leadership of CST Artistic Director Edward Hall and taking its inspiration from Shakespeare’s own company and CST’s roots as the Shakespeare Repertory, a company of 14 actors perform both The Winter’s Tale and A Midsummer Night’s Dream, two of Shakespeare’s most beguiling fairy tales. This double header of productions makes for a thrilling theatrical experience, with two beautiful plays exploring the formidable power of love, laughter and forgiveness.

title: Reconnecting with the Earth: A Yoga Nidrā Practice for Deep Rest
description:
An invitation to rest, ground, and be held by the Earth
This deeply restorative class offers space to pause, soften, and come home — to your body, your breath, and the steady presence of the Earth beneath you. We begin with gentle, optional movement and/or soothing pranayama to support settling and ease, before resting into an extended Yoga Nidrā practice.
Yoga Nidrā, often translated as “yogic sleep,” is a guided meditative experience that supports deep rest while maintaining conscious awareness. In this class, we dedicate our practice to reconnecting with the Earth and the natural world, inviting you to sense yourself as part of our surrounding environment through embodied awareness, breath, and guided visualization. The intention is to gently cultivate a felt sense of grounding, belonging, and renewed connection with our planet — at your own pace, in your own time.
This class is an invitation to rest, restore, and reconnect, especially during times of stress, grief, or transition. All bodies, nervous systems, and levels of experience are welcome.

title: Raise the Red Lantern
description:
DIRECTED BY
Yimou Zhang
WRITTEN BY
Tong Su,
Ni Zhen
STARRING
Gong Li,
Jingwu Ma,
Saifei He
Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father's death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.
“As visually striking as it is dramatically effective,” Zhang Yimou’s Academy Award-nominated Raise the Red Lantern sumptuously captures 1920s China while “subtly exploring the politics of power and control” (Janet Maslin, The New York Times). One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.
The 4K restoration of Raise the Red Lantern was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong - Bologna).

title: Tommy Davidson
description:
Tommy Davidson's Bio
Tommy Davidson’s exceptional range – from stand-up comedy and acting to versatile music accomplishments – have earned him a reputation as an extraordinary performer who delivers no matter the arena. Best known as one of the stars of the hit television show In Living Color, Davidson’s visibility has allowed him to become a household name known for his innovative talent.
Davidson started his career as a standup comedian in Washington DC, earning an ardent following. Spotted by major concert promoters, he was first booked as the opening act for Patti LaBelle, Kenny G and Luther Vandross. It wasn’t long before he came to Hollywood and was headlining the biggest rooms and met Robert Townsend. This led to his first national tv appearance and starring role in Partners in Crime, the conduit to Keenan Ivory Wayans, who proved instrumental in Davidson’s career by offering him an opportunity to audition.
Davidson starred in Disney Channel’s beloved animated series The Proud Family (2001-05) and recently returned to topline their new hit, “The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder” (Disney +) to rave reviews. Other 2022 guest starring credits include CBS comedy series The Neighborhood; standout roles on VH1’s hit A Black Lady Sketch Show; the Nick Cannon-directed TV movie Miracles Across 125th Street, BET+’s The Ms. Pat Show and the Netflix special Sarah Cooper: Everything’s Fine.
The multihyphenate is perhaps best known for starring in the groundbreaking sketch comedy series In Living Color and becoming a standout with his impressions of Sammy Davis Jr., Michael Jackson and other entertainment icons. His performance on the series resulted in three Showtime specials: On Strength of New York, Illin’ in Philly, and Takin’ it to DC. Davidson also hosted and starred in the network’s Chocolate Sundaes Comedy Show, as well as three seasons of ABC’s Vacation Creation.
Davidson voiced the series regular role of Cream Corn in the Adult Swim action-comedy spoof Black Dynamite, and has also made multiple guest appearances on shows like MTV’s Wild ‘N Out, BET’s Real Husbands of Hollywood and ABC’s Celebrity Wife Swap. He also recently headlined The Off Color Comedy Tour with Keenan Ivory Wayans, Shawn Wayans and David Alan Grier, and co-headlines with Katt Williams, Mike Epps and Martin Lawrence to sell out large venue audiences.
Davidson’s feature credits include Spike Lee’s Bamboozled, Morgan Creek’s Juwanna Mann, Ace Ventura II: When Nature Calls opposite Jim Carrey, and Strictly Business opposite Halle Berry among others. He also recently starred in the feature documentaries I Am Comic opposite Tim Allen and Lewis Black, and Dying Laughing alongside Jamie Foxx, Kevin Hart, Amy Schumer and Sarah Silverman.
His most recent critically lauded music duets include Sweet Reunion with multi-Grammy winner Dave Koz and I Know with A-list saxophonist, Richard Elliot.
Kensington Books published Davidson’s memoir Living in Color: What’s Funny about Me, recounting his personal triumphs after having been abandoned as in infant in 2020 achieving historic sales.
